top_story.headline: Dolores Huerta Action Fund tells the FEC its 2024 independent-expenditure reports may be overstated
top_story.dek: Counsel's review suggests general overhead was reported as independent-expenditure cost; amendments are delayed because the filing account is no longer active.
paragraphs: The Dolores Huerta Action Fund filed a Form 99 on October 3 (letter dated October 2) to Patrick Harkins, a Senior Campaign Finance and Reviewing Analyst at the Federal Election Commission. It concerns the group's October Quarterly 2024 (07/01/2024–09/30/2024) and Year-End 2024 (10/01/2024–12/31/2024) reports.

Outside counsel's ongoing review found that certain amounts may have been reported on an overinclusive basis, including legal, compliance and administrative costs, expenses shared with nonfederal or candidate-free voter engagement, and pay for staff who did both qualifying and other work. The group says general overhead not directly attributable to a specific express-advocacy communication should not count toward an independent expenditure's reported cost.

The letter adds that the compliance-software account used to prepare the original reports is no longer active, so the reports must be recreated in a new account before amendments can be filed. It asks the FEC's Reports Analysis Division for additional time and was signed by Tracey Frazier Wigglesworth of The Political Law Group. The letter gives no dollar figures or deadline.

sections.headline: Four below-threshold statements and one amendment-delay request
paragraphs: Five new miscellaneous Form 99 submissions surfaced, all filed 10/03. Four are small campaigns stating they fall under the $5,000 reporting threshold. None is from a sitting member of Congress.

items: Dolores Huerta Action Fund (independent-expenditure group, filed 10/03) — asks the FEC to allow more time to amend its October Quarterly 2024 and Year-End 2024 reports after outside counsel found independent expenditures may have been reported on an overinclusive basis. Filing.

Kyle Haigler (Democrat, SC-6, challenger status not listed by FEC), committee Kyle Haigler for Congress — two near-identical statements, filed 10/03, that it has not raised or spent more than $5,000 as of September 30, 2026 and so has not met the reporting threshold. Statement one; statement two.

Brandon Conceicao (Other party, NH-2, challenger), committee Brandon Conceicao for Congress — filed 10/03 to state for the public record that it did not raise or spend more than $5,000 by September 30, 2026 and was not required to file the October Quarterly. Filing.
Robert William Whitehead (Green, NC-8, challenger), committee Whitehead for Congress NC — filed 10/03, declares the committee has not reached the $5,000 threshold for financial reports. Filing.
